newsitem.title: MEXICO: Guillermo nears hurricane strength off Mexico.
newsitem.headline: Guillermo nears hurricane strength off Mexico.

text.p: Tropical storm Guillermo, picking up steam off Mexico's Pacific coast, is seen converting into a hurricane in the few next hours, the National Meterological Service said Friday.
Guillermo is currently centered 310 miles (495 km) south southwest of the famous tourist resort Acapulco, packing sustained winds of 70 miles per hour (mph) (110 km/h) and gusts of 88 mph (140 km/h).
"It is expected that Tropical Storm Guillermo continues to pick up steam to become a hurricane in the course of the (Friday) morning," it added.

Moving west northwesterly, Guillermo is seen centered 325 miles (520 km) south southwest of the resort of Zihuatanejo in Guerrero state at 1300 local (1800 GMT), moving up a gear to produce maximum sustained winds of 81 mph (130 km/h) and gusts of 97 mph (155 km/h).
Guillermo is currently dumping heavy rains over the states of Guerrero and Michoacan, both farming states. TV network Televisa reported overnight floods in Acapulco.
Shipping warnings were extended along all Mexico's Pacific coast because of the rains, waves and sea swells whipped up by the weather system, the service said.
